summary_for_children: Al-Masad tells of Abu Lahab and his wife, who opposed the Prophet (peace be upon him), and that wealth did not help them.
environment_concept: A dusk road past an abandoned heap of chests and coins that does no good to anyone, and a bundle of firewood tied with a twisted rope. No person is shown, and the Fire of 111:3 is not pictured.
architecture_and_scenery: Dusty chests and scattered coins, a firewood bundle with a rope of twisted fibre.

areas.name: Wealth That Will Not Avail
areas.description: An abandoned heap of chests and coins half sunk in sand: wealth that did not help its owner.

areas.name: Firewood and Rope
areas.description: A bundle of firewood tied with a rope of twisted fibre (111:4-5). No person is shown.

depiction_rules: No prophet, person or representation of Allah is shown. Unseen realities are never pictured. Interactive activities are labelled as adaptations.

unique_world.visual_theme: A date grove with an old well whose rope has frayed, and bundles of palm fibre

primary_mechanic.text: Twist three strands of palm fibre four times each, all the same way (a strand the other way is refused); lay them together the opposite way (the same way springs apart and is refused); then tie on the bucket and lower it at the well. Abu Lahab and his wife are never shown; the warning is read only.

secondary_activities: his wealth will not avail him (111:1-2, read)
unique_world.narrative_structure: A reading at the grove gate, the rope and the well, then a reading among the palms
environment_behaviour: each twisted strand appears on the bench; the rope hangs in the well once made
unique_world.learning_objective: Know that wealth and gains do not avail one who opposes the truth (111:2)

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: A Warning Against Arrogance
story_library.children_narration: Abu Lahab strongly opposed Prophet Muhammad's message. Surah Al-Masad warns about his opposition and that of his wife. The surah reminds us that wealth, family position, or influence do not make harmful actions right.

world_idea.title: The House of Pride
world_idea.description: Explore a symbolic historic courtyard and learn about the consequences of arrogance and opposition to truth. Present the original account through narration, not fictional reenactment.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: Abu Lahab and his wife are not shown and nothing is acted out; the warning is a reading.
